page_title: Vauta — Free AI meeting notes and minutes that stay on your Mac

sources.entry: Vauta - Open-source meeting notes app that transcribes any call on device, tells speakers apart and writes cited minutes with Apple Intelligence or your own local model server. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/MaquinaTech/Vauta) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Vauta
summary.one_liner: Vauta is a free, open-source Mac app that records any call on your Mac, transcribes it on-device, and writes minutes with decisions, tasks and open questions.
use_cases: Taking minutes of work calls without a bot joining
Extracting decisions, tasks and owners from meetings
Keeping meeting transcripts private on your own Mac
Transcribing recorded audio or video files into meeting notes
Searching across past meetings and documents by meaning
summary.what_it_does: Vauta captures your microphone as the speaker 'Me' and the call audio as 'Others', working with any call app on the Mac without a bot joining. It transcribes audio on the device with Apple's speech recognition, tells speakers apart, and lets you name them once. Minutes list decisions, tasks with owner and date, and open questions, with each item quoting the transcript; unsupported items are marked unconfirmed. Transcripts and minutes are stored encrypted (AES-256) with the key in the Keychain, and audio is not saved to disk. Output can be exported as Markdown, PDF, subtitles or JSON, and audio or video files can be imported.
notable: Open source under Apache-2.0 with no account or telemetry; no bot joins the call
Minutes are written by Apple Intelligence on the Mac or by a user-run local model server; internet model servers are refused
Connected memory: searches transcripts, minutes and PDF/Word/Excel/PowerPoint files together, with optional semantic search (574 MB download)
Reports benchmarks such as 9.5% speaker error rate and 7.6% word error rate in Spanish, with stated test limits
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon; no Windows or web version
System-audio capture has only been tested in real calls in Safari so far
